Me2U MTN Fraud

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Me2U is an app on MTN cell phone banking but fraudsters are adding their numbers to MTN accounts without the knowledge of the owner of the account and they only find out that money has been deducted when they get their month end invoice. All calls to the MTN fraud line go unassisted- is this an inside job and if not why is MTN fraud department not assisting their customers?

Summary:
The latest fraud within MTN is the Me2U money scam when fraudsters are able to add their number to your account and bypass your spend limit without your knowledge . They get sent the OTP of the main account holder without their knowledge so they unaware that it is happening until they receive their account at the end of the month. If you call in during the month to see if anyone is spending on your account they can’t tell you, because they only looking at the number you have called in on and you don’t have the OPT of the fraudulent number on your account. Even if you reduce your spend limit to 0 MTN independently sets a credit limit on your account which they do by running a credit check, so the fraudster can spend up to the limit MTN has given you. They are suspending peoples accounts for not paying these fraudulently spent amounts despite customers reporting the fraudulent added numbers.

Further information:
People have lost up to R25000 and when they report it to the fraud line they get an automated response and told it been investigated and they will get back to them in 3 days. They never do. When they call in and tell people to block the fraudulently added number they told they can’t and the supervisor is in a meeting and will call back, they never do. When they initially call in are report the fraud they told to open a case at the police station, but even with a case number nothing happens. If you call the fraud hotline it doesn’t get answered. People are desperate, so the use the MTN facebook page to complain. Then they get a DM asking for their OTP and all their details and which is what the fraudsters already have access to and something they should not reveal. It looks like an inside job and if it isn’t why isn’t MTN doing everything they can to assist their customers like the bank fraud lines. It appears that their various systems are no co-ordinated, even The MTN “Champions” aren’t able to intervene. We have many people caught and MTN is not assisting or reversing these fraudulent spends even when people report it immediately.

Script:


Script: Some MTN customers got the shock of their lives
Link: when they get their bills at the end of the month only to discover that some random number has been added to their account and data and money has been transferred without them even knowing
Script: Over the last 7 months Cyber criminals have breached the MTN system and accessed people's accounts. First they increase the spend limits, and within seconds transfer data, MTN rewards and do money transfers, to unreced numbers making them untraceable
Stephanie “ All of a sudden I started receiving these SMS that my spending limit has all of a sudden being changed to nine thousand nine hundred and ninety nine rand. It was within minutes from there I just received SMS saying that someone has transferred two hundred rands of airtime to a number that I don't know.
Script: Stephanie Marais’s quick thinking saved her losing anymore, she ripped out the sim card and managed to stop R8000 worth of data being transferred
Stephanie “And I immediately phoned the fraud number and the lady on the other end to see that she can't do anything from her side. I had to email MTN and open a case basically for fraud., I just received an out of office back. And I went into the Paarl office the next morning and they opened a fraud case. And then everyone asked me, did I receive an OTP or not? And I have to this day, I never received an OTP for any of those transactions
Script It's been 3 months of endless stress, and damage to her credit record
Stephanie It basically took a month for that ticket to be closed. And they just said it was the customer's own fault.
Script: Ansie Van Deventer is a 77 years old pensioner. Her daughter took her into the local MTN Bayside store in Cape Town to upgrade her phone contract.
Jacoline” We explicitly asked that it's only three hundred and sixty nine , it doesn't exceed that limit so that my mother can stay in her budget
Link: It looks like the store is they have closed up shop but this is where they came to upgrade her contract. But while MTN was setting up her phone unbeknown to Ann her credit limit was increased to over R8000, and the very next day, thats is when it all began
Jacoline “It’s a number we do not know its a me 2u Money transfer and they deducted one hundred and seventy two thousand ninety one cents daily from the 9th until the 16th of May
Script: The criminals frequently change themselves to the main account holder, so people don't get SMS alerting them to the fraud. Ansie and her daughter don’t use the MTNapp, so they were none the wiser until the invoice arrived. When they returned to the Bayside Store, they were told there was nothing they could do, and spent several weeks trying to get answers from the fraud department. They even tried cancelling the contract, but the only control they had was to cancel the debit order, in the hopes that would get MTN’s attention, but they just cut off her calls
Masa: What kind of impact is the stress having
Jacoline A lot, she doesn't know what to do anymore
Script: MTN has 32 million customers, that’s a vast amount of personal information, and makes it a target for cyber criminals - says Jackie O Sullivan MTN South Africa for Corporate Affairs executive
Jacqui “We are constantly facing a deluge of attacks from cyber criminals. And when I say it deluge we're talking about 15000 spam emails that we block, every single day five thousand eight hundred different attacks on the different MTN sites.
Script; In December 2020 MTN noticed an increase in fraudulent activities, and brought in the hawks to investigate, and the company is not ruling out insider collusion
Jacqui “ So when they came on to our systems, they went looking for I.D. numbers. They were actually copying and pasting into our system, trying to find matches. Once they found a match then they could perpetrate types of fraud, for instance, adding another line to your account or sending your data to somebody else.
Script: But somehow that message wasn't getting out to the call centres or instore staff
Link: When customers go to MTN stores to try and get help the staff in store tell them there is nothing they can do and the customers should call the 135 fraud line, when they do call that number they get no answer. Emailing the fraud department they only get an automatic response saying the problem will be dealt with in 48 hours, and all the while the scamsters is stripping their account
Jackie: This was a deplorable service for which we have profusely apologized, and what this spike has shown us is that we need a much bigger fraud team, which we have already put in place that is already acting. What we need is to make sure that there are much simpler processes to help customers.
Warren “Now it says my usage limit has been extended to R18 600
Script: Cyber criminals hit Warren and Kim Wright. Armed with their contract details Kim was easily reassured
Warren “The phone rang at about 4:00 in the afternoon…., he said, Hello, Kim, I'm calling from the MTN store. There's somebody standing here wanting to do a SIM swap on this number. She kinda replied to the guy saying, no, no, no, definitely not you, you cannot do SIMswap on that number. he said, I've just sent you a number to authorize the cancellation. She then read him the number he said the system was slow and that number didn't work. You asked for the number again.. He said there was still a glitch on the system. He asked for a third number. When I heard that, I then said what numbers are you giving because MTN has a pin that i am supposed to give them that opens up all the information to them
Upsound-I have got a code that I give them
Link: To Warrens horror he discovered his credit limit was extended to R18 000 without his knowledge or consent
Warren: the following morning we went through to the MTN store in Boksburg, she set the limit on my phone to fourteen thousand eight hundred and forty seven rand or something.
Masa: Did you ask her for a limit of fourteen thousand
Warren: well she told me that that's what had been spent. So she then locked it that they couldn't spend any further money, but subsequently as we stand the bill is standing on R26 000.
Script: Accepting they made the initial mistake of sharing the password Warren is baffled how MTN approved an R18 000 credit limit without any questions
Warren “ So the fact that you can transfer four thousand rand data and four thousand and data , another two thousand rand data out of a cell phone contract, that's a three hundred top up. And it doesn't raise alarm bells at MTN. That is scary. And they are trading recklessly that is my opinion
Script: Kim didn’t have MTN app and was told if she loaded it she could stop the fraud and monitor what was happening, but to her horror the criminals were still at it, setting the credit limit, had done nothing to protect them
Warren: My wife got a message to data sharing switched on, she went into the phone when she switched it of, we could see the icon move back to on.so that man is in our app or woman, I suppose. And there's nothing that we can do about it.
Masa: And you're the main account holder. But you weren't able to see this?
Warren: I wasn't able to see this, it's like an invasion. This man is now in our app and there is no way for us to logg him out of it to to this day. I think he can still just go in and resume the session.
Stephanie- Once you have gone into it once it stays on your phone and you don't need a password. On the evening that had happened, I just try to change back my settings from ten thousand rand to I think you can only make it one rand. I wasn't able to, like, basically just kick me out the whole time and then they actually only were able to change it back at the branch. So I'm not sure how you or I you're supposed to change any of those settings when it's not possible for you to change it back and then they just don't give you any guidance.
Jacqui: First of all in the event of OTP scam like that, the first thing you can do is that you can immediately go into the MTN app, you can delete the app Reload it and reset your username and password.
Masa: I'm sorry, Jacqui, I'm going to have to stop you there, because with everyone that we spoke to, we checked their app and they were able to go in and out of it. The question is why isn't there a password? Every single time you log onto the My MTN app as you would with a banking app for instance
Jacqui: There's a fine line to walk when dealing with apps, it's important for us to be able to make them as accessible as possible so that people can very simply and easily do their transactions and do whatever is required in the simplest way possible .But we are having to look at biometrics and facial scans.
Script: The inability to get a response out of MTN left Debi Gerber vulnerable to another scam. Her husband bought a R20000 phone which stopped working within two months. They returned it to the MTN store to be repaired or replaced, but for 4 months they couldn’t get any answers no matter what channels they followed.
Debi: Eventually, out of desperation, we resorted to social media, so we went on to the MTN South Africa, a Facebook page which has the blue ticks, so it's the official page. And then we got a response and we were so thrilled. After about a few minutes after MTN, South Africa's response to me on their page, I received a direct message from Natasha MTNza
Script: But it was scammer who watches MTN’s facebook page for complaints
Masa “How quickly did Natasha respond to your complaint
Debi “When she contacted me, it was 13 minutes from the time I'd first put the post up to the time she contacted me.
Script: Natasha MTNSA sometimes also going by the name of Michelle MTNSA has insider information
Debi: She provided us with personal details that I hadn't provided to her at all, the MTN account number, our residential address, the last four digits of my husband's bank account that the debit order comes from, as well as the debit order amount.
Script: The scam was elaborate and convincing; they would be refunded and the phone replaced but first they needed to settle the original contract. All communication was on what appeared to be a MTN business whatsapp line.
Debi: Then she told me that she would refund an initial amount of nine thousand rand. And the following day, she said, oh, dear, the system froze when she was making the payment it has gone through twice, I should just check the account, and sure enough, there was eighteen thousand rand into the account. And there again, I'm impressed because MTN is refunded me a nine thousand rand fantastic right but now they have overpaid me so now I need to refund that money back.
Script. Using their FIKA details Natasha was opening Capfin and Wonga loans in both Debi and her husband's name.
Debi They gave a scammer money on our name
Script: They are now liable for those loans and are R45 600 out of pocket, and had to hire a private investigator
Debi From the 8th of December of handing in that phone for repair or replacement, until today, we have not received anything, any resolution from MTN
Warren: I don't know where to turn it. It's sad to think that we feel this is a victory, carte blanche has come to sit and talk to us about this.
Stephanie When you guys submitted my case to them, they actually phoned me this afternoon to say, no, it's all been sorted. All of a sudden
Masa: it's no longer your fault
Stephanie. Now, all of a sudden, it's not my fault
Masa: How are any of your customers who had their details compromised, supposed to trust MTN that this won't happen again?
Jacqui We don't know if there are other frauds out there that we're not immediately aware of, that customers haven't already reported to us. So we're encouraging customers to have a look at their invoices, make sure they've got the very latest version of any app there's a specific e-mail address that's been set up that is being dealt with by this enlarged enforcement team specifically make sure that we cut down those delays and we put the customers directly in touch with the fraud investigations rather than making them go through any circuitous route whatsoever
Script: After our intervention, Ansie's fraudulent line and the charges associated with it, were removed, and she was finally able to cancel her contract. MTN then removed the R26000 against Warren’s account, and he promptly reloaded the app, setting all the limits to zero.

Jacqui We don't know if there are other frauds out there that we're not immediately aware of, that customers haven't already reported to us. So we're encouraging customers to have a look at their invoices, make sure they've got the very latest version of any app there's a specific e-mail address that's been set up that is being dealt with by this enlarged enforcement team specifically make sure that we cut down those delays and we put the customers directly in touch with the fraud investigations rather than making them go through any circuitous route whatsoever Script: After our intervention, Ansie's fraudulent line and the charges associated with it, were removed, and she was finally able to cancel her contract. MTN then removed the R26000 against Warren’s account, and he promptly reloaded the app, setting all the limits to zero.

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Me2U is an app on MTN cell phone banking but fraudsters are adding their numbers to MTN accounts without the knowledge of the owner of the account and they only find out that money has been deducted when they get their month end invoice. All calls to the MTN fraud line go unassisted- is this an inside job and if not why is MTN fraud department not assisting their customers?
metadata.Summary: The latest fraud within MTN is the Me2U money scam when fraudsters are able to add their number to your account and bypass your spend limit without your knowledge . They get sent the OTP of the main account holder without their knowledge so they unaware that it is happening until they receive their account at the end of the month. If you call in during the month to see if anyone is spending on your account they can’t tell you, because they only looking at the number you have called in on and you don’t have the OPT of the fraudulent number on your account. Even if you reduce your spend limit to 0 MTN independently sets a credit limit on your account which they do by running a credit check, so the fraudster can spend up to the limit MTN has given you. They are suspending peoples accounts for not paying these fraudulently spent amounts despite customers reporting the fraudulent added numbers.
metadata.Further information: People have lost up to R25000 and when they report it to the fraud line they get an automated response and told it been investigated and they will get back to them in 3 days. They never do. When they call in and tell people to block the fraudulently added number they told they can’t and the supervisor is in a meeting and will call back, they never do. When they initially call in are report the fraud they told to open a case at the police station, but even with a case number nothing happens. If you call the fraud hotline it doesn’t get answered. People are desperate, so the use the MTN facebook page to complain. Then they get a DM asking for their OTP and all their details and which is what the fraudsters already have access to and something they should not reveal. It looks like an inside job and if it isn’t why isn’t MTN doing everything they can to assist their customers like the bank fraud lines. It appears that their various systems are no co-ordinated, even The MTN “Champions” aren’t able to intervene. We have many people caught and MTN is not assisting or reversing these fraudulent spends even when people report it immediately.
